policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders 'by his guidance' with no note attached to this unit. 'Guidance' is a mass noun in English and carries no number, so it renders the ketiv singular בתחבולתו and the qere plural בְּתַחְבּוּלֹתָ֣יו alike; the ASV wording therefore distinguishes neither. Both readings remain compatible and the qere base fallback carries the projection.
